title: Capital Gains Tax on Stocks, ETFs, and Equity MFs Explained

faq.q: What is the holding period for equity shares and equity mutual funds to qualify as long-term?
faq.a: For listed equity shares, equity-oriented mutual funds, and equity ETFs, the holding period must be more than 12 months to qualify as a long-term asset.

faq.q: Is indexation benefit available for Long-Term Capital Gains on equities?
faq.a: No, the benefit of indexation is not available for Long-Term Capital Gains arising from the sale of listed equity shares, equity-oriented mutual funds, or equity ETFs.

faq.q: Can I adjust capital losses against other income sources?
faq.a: No, capital losses can only be set off against capital gains. They cannot be set off against other income sources like salary, house property income, or business income.

faq.q: What happens if I have Long-Term Capital Losses?
faq.a: Long-Term Capital Losses (LTCL) can only be set off against Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG). If not fully adjusted in the current year, they can be carried forward for up to 8 subsequent assessment years, provided you file your ITR on time.

faq.q: Are dividends from equity mutual funds or stocks taxable?
faq.a: Yes, dividends received from Indian companies or equity mutual funds are fully taxable in the hands of the recipient at their applicable income tax slab rates.

faq.q: Do I need to pay Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on these transactions?
faq.a: Yes, Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied on the purchase and sale of equity shares, equity-oriented mutual funds, and equity ETFs on recognised stock exchanges in India. This is a prerequisite for availing the concessional tax rates under Section 111A and 112A.
